design:
Tier 1: UI plus the CLI's native window; no Hub code, no migration. The bundle reaches :8000 on reload; the native bridge needs the CLI to relaunch the app.
D1. hub/ui/src/lib/notify/: a pure classify(type, data) -> {kind, text} | null, and a Notifier (state: unseen count, burst window, prefs) driven by an injected clock, sound player and bridge, so the tests drive it without a DOM audio stack. useNotifications() mounts it once in App.tsx through useSSE(listener).
D2. Sound: lib/sound/agentweave-sound.js is the brand file copied verbatim (UMD: it sets globalThis.AgentWeaveSound when there is no module); one AudioContext, created lazily, resumed on the first pointerdown/keydown for the browser case. Gains: master gain = volume x 0.35 in front, volume x 0.7 behind.
D3. Focus is document.hasFocus() at the moment of the event, with window focus/blur listeners to clear the count; visibilityState alone stays 'visible' for a window that is merely covered.
D4. Native bridge: cli._AppWindowApi passed as js_api to both create_window calls. attention(n) -> window.set_title + FlashWindowEx(FLASHW_TRAY|FLASHW_TIMERNOFG) on the visible top-level window owned by this PID (found with EnumWindows, never by title alone); sound(enabled) writes app-window/sound.json. The UI calls window.pywebview?.api when present and only sets document.title otherwise. Spike 2026-10-23: js_api survives load_url; set_title and FlashWindowEx work.
D5. Autoplay: the CLI sets WEBVIEW2_ADDITIONAL_BROWSER_ARGUMENTS to '--autoplay-policy=no-user-gesture-required' (appended to any existing value, and repeating pywebview's own --disable-features=ElasticOverscroll in case the variable replaces its arguments) before webview.start. Spike: suspended without it, running with it.
D6. Preferences: localStorage 'agentweave-notify' {sound, volume, kinds:{ask,fail,done}}; defaults sound on, volume 0.8, ask and fail on, done off. Settings > General gains a 'Sound and notifications' group; a change to the switch calls bridge.sound(enabled).
D7. Toasts reuse lib/toast (Radix): a burst updates its open toast in place rather than stacking, through a new toast store update(id, input).
problem: The operator decided the notification design in the thread lab on 2026-10-23 (toast and a quiet sound in front; all projects notify) and the sound set exists (brand/sound/agentweave-sound.js: ask, done, fail), but nothing in the app plays a sound or calls attention. A question an agent asks while the window is behind waits silently until the operator happens to look; the opening sound is the only sound AgentWeave makes.

requirements.rationale: Thread lab, 2026-10-23: sounds by default for 'needs you' and 'stalled or failed'; 'done' is off by default.
requirements.statement: The app MUST play the brand's ask sound when an agent asks the operator a question or requests a permission, and the fail sound when a stall is recorded, a run fails, a message chain is suspended or a loop stops for any reason but a drained queue; a loop that drained its queue is done, which is silent unless the operator turns it on.
The app MUST show a toast naming the event's project and what happened, with an action that opens that project, and play the sound at a quiet level, when its window has focus.

requirements.rationale: Identity record §7: window in the background gets the sound, a count in the title and a flashing taskbar button.
requirements.statement: The app MUST, when its window does not have focus, play the sound at the normal level, prefix the title with the count of unseen notifications as '(n) AgentWeave', and in the native app window flash the taskbar button; the count and the flash MUST clear when the window regains focus.

requirements.rationale: 'One sound at most every few seconds; a burst is one sound and one grouped toast.'
requirements.statement: The app MUST play at most one notification sound per 4 seconds, and MUST group the events arriving within that window into one toast, the more urgent kind (fail over ask over done) choosing the sound.
The app MUST notify for events from every project on the Hub, not only the selected one, and label each with its project's name.

requirements.rationale: brand/sound/README.md: 'the operator can turn sound off'; the handoff asked that AGENTWEAVE_SOUND and the app setting agree.
requirements.statement: The operator MUST be able to turn notification sound off, set its volume and choose which kinds sound, in Settings, and the choice MUST survive a relaunch; turning sound off MUST also silence the opening sound of the native app, and AGENTWEAVE_SOUND=0 MUST still silence the opening whatever the setting says.

requirements.rationale: Spike 2026-10-23: a page's AudioContext in pywebview's WebView2 starts suspended, so an operator who opens the app and walks away would never hear the call this change exists for; --autoplay-policy=no-user-gesture-required makes it running.
requirements.statement: The native app window MUST let a notification sound play before the operator has interacted with the page; in a plain browser tab the sound MUST become available on the operator's first click or key press.

requirements.rationale: The first shipped opening came from a second synth that drifted out of tune; the brand keeps one source.
requirements.statement: The app MUST play its notification sounds from a copy of brand/sound/agentweave-sound.js that is byte-identical to it, and a test MUST fail when the two differ.

in_scope: A notifier in hub/ui that listens to the one instance-wide SSE stream and classifies events: ask = question_asked, permission_requested; fail = stall_recorded, run_failed, queue_chain_suspended, loop_stopped for any reason but a drained queue; done = loop_stopped because its queue drained
Window in front (document.hasFocus()): a toast naming the project and what happened, with an action that opens that project, and the sound at a quiet level
Window behind: the sound at the normal level, '(n) AgentWeave' in the title, and in the native app window a flashing taskbar button; both clear when the window regains focus
At most one sound per 4 s; events arriving inside that window join one grouped toast ('3 things in <project>' or '3 things across 2 projects')
Operator preferences in localStorage (persistent since f577b6b): sound on/off, volume, per-kind toggles (ask on, fail on, done off), in Settings > General

The native window: a js_api bridge (attention(count) sets the native title and FlashWindowEx; sound(enabled) writes ~/.agentweave/hub/app-window/sound.json, which the CLI reads before the opening sound), and the WebView2 autoplay policy that lets a sound play before the operator has clicked
The UI plays the brand synth itself: hub/ui/src/lib/sound/agentweave-sound.js is a byte-identical copy of brand/sound/agentweave-sound.js, held so by a test
out_of_scope: Operating-system toast notifications (Windows Action Center) and the Notification API: the operator picked an in-app toast; a spike decides later whether the OS toast is worth it
Review and merge needs (a task awaiting the operator's approval): no single event says so today; filed to the backlog
The Docker app path (no native window) beyond the browser behaviour

summary: When an agent needs the operator (a question, a permission) or work stalls or fails, in any project on the Hub, the app says so with the brand's struck-glass sound: a toast and a quiet sound when its window is in front; the sound, a count in the title and a flashing taskbar button when it is behind. One sound per burst, done is off by default, and the operator can mute, set the volume and pick which kinds sound.
